subject: mathematics
label: Adds numerators and denominators straight across
label_ms: Menambah pengangka dan penyebut secara terus
description: Treats a fraction as two independent whole numbers, so 1/2 + 1/3 becomes 2/5 instead of 5/6.
correctReasoning: Fractions can only be added once the parts are the same size, so both must be rewritten over a common denominator.
diagnosticQuestion: Ali ate 1/2 of a pizza and Siti ate 1/3 of the same pizza. How much did they eat altogether?
remediationHint: Fold or shade two identical rectangles into halves and thirds, then cut both into sixths and count.

subject: mathematics
label: Believes a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction
label_ms: Menganggap penyebut lebih besar bermakna pecahan lebih besar
description: Applies whole-number ordering to denominators, concluding 1/8 is greater than 1/3 because 8 is greater than 3.
correctReasoning: The denominator counts how many pieces the whole is cut into, so more pieces means each piece is smaller.
diagnosticQuestion: Which is larger, 1/3 of a chocolate bar or 1/8 of the same bar? Explain.
remediationHint: Cut one paper strip into 3 equal parts and an identical strip into 8, then compare a single piece from each.

subject: mathematics
label: Makes equivalent fractions by adding instead of multiplying
label_ms: Menghasilkan pecahan setara dengan menambah, bukan mendarab
description: Adds the same number to numerator and denominator, so 2/3 is thought equal to 3/4.
correctReasoning: Equivalence preserves the ratio, so both parts must be scaled by the same factor, not shifted by the same amount.
diagnosticQuestion: Is 2/3 the same amount as 3/4? Show your reasoning with a diagram.
remediationHint: Compare 2/3 and 3/4 on the same number line before discussing any rule.

subject: mathematics
label: Inverts the wrong fraction when dividing
label_ms: Menyongsangkan pecahan yang salah semasa membahagi
description: Flips the first fraction rather than the divisor when applying the reciprocal rule.
correctReasoning: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor only.
diagnosticQuestion: How many half-metre ribbons can be cut from a 3/4 metre ribbon?
remediationHint: Ask how many halves fit inside 3/4 before touching the algorithm; the answer must be more than 1.

subject: mathematics
label: Reads the word of as divide in fraction problems
description: Computes 2/5 of 30 by dividing by the fraction, losing track of the operation and getting an answer larger than the whole.
correctReasoning: The word of signals multiplication; dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a larger answer, which fails the reasonableness check.
diagnosticQuestion: A class of 30 pupils has 2/5 girls. How many girls are there?
remediationHint: Estimate first: 2/5 is less than half, so the answer must be less than 15.

subject: mathematics
label: Thinks more decimal places means a larger number
label_ms: Menganggap lebih banyak tempat perpuluhan bermakna nombor lebih besar
description: Compares decimals by digit count, concluding 0.125 is greater than 0.5.
correctReasoning: Decimal size is decided place by place from the left, not by how many digits follow the point.
diagnosticQuestion: Order these from smallest to largest: 0.5, 0.125, 0.36
remediationHint: Line the numbers up on a place-value chart and pad with trailing zeros.

subject: mathematics
label: Right-aligns digits instead of the decimal point
label_ms: Menyusun digit dari kanan, bukan pada titik perpuluhan
description: Adds or subtracts decimals as if they were whole numbers, so 2.5 + 0.75 is mis-aligned and gives 1.00 or 0.100.
correctReasoning: Only digits of the same place value may be combined, so the decimal points must line up.
diagnosticQuestion: Calculate 2.5 + 0.75 and explain how you lined up the numbers.
remediationHint: Rewrite 2.5 as 2.50 first so both numbers have the same number of decimal places.

subject: mathematics
label: Believes multiplying always makes a number bigger
label_ms: Menganggap pendaraban sentiasa menghasilkan nombor lebih besar
description: Expects 8 x 0.4 to exceed 8, and rejects a correct answer of 3.2 as impossible.
correctReasoning: Multiplying by a number less than 1 scales down, the same way taking a fraction of a quantity does.
diagnosticQuestion: Without calculating exactly, is 8 x 0.4 more or less than 8? Why?
remediationHint: Link 0.4 to 4/10 and ask for four-tenths of 8 using a bar model.

subject: mathematics
label: Rounds using the wrong digit
description: Rounds 3.648 to one decimal place by working from the last digit inwards, giving 3.7 by way of 3.65.
correctReasoning: Rounding to a place looks only at the single digit immediately to its right.
diagnosticQuestion: Round 3.648 to one decimal place and say which digit you used to decide.
remediationHint: Mark 3.648 on a number line between 3.6 and 3.7 and see which end is nearer.

subject: mathematics
label: Confuses percentage of an amount with percentage off
label_ms: Mengelirukan peratus daripada jumlah dengan peratus diskaun
description: Reports the discount itself as the final price, answering RM 12 instead of RM 68 for 15% off RM 80.
correctReasoning: The discount must be subtracted from the original price to give the amount actually paid.
diagnosticQuestion: A shirt costs RM 80 with 15% off. How much does Aina pay?
remediationHint: Ask what is left after the discount: 100% minus 15% is 85% of RM 80.

subject: mathematics
label: Reverses a percentage increase by subtracting the same percentage
label_ms: Menyongsangkan kenaikan peratus dengan menolak peratus yang sama
description: Takes 20% off the increased price to recover the original, not recognising that the two percentages act on different bases.
studentExample: Price after a 20% rise is RM 120, so the original was RM 96
correctReasoning: The increased price is 120% of the original, so the original is the new price divided by 1.2.
diagnosticQuestion: After a 20% increase a bag costs RM 120. What was the original price?
remediationHint: Draw a bar of 100% and add a 20% block; the whole bar is 120%, not the starting point.

subject: mathematics
label: Adds successive percentages together
description: Treats two successive 10% discounts as a single 20% discount, ignoring that the second applies to an already reduced price.
correctReasoning: Successive percentages multiply: 0.9 x 0.9 = 0.81, which is 19% off in total.
diagnosticQuestion: A RM 100 item is reduced by 10%, then by another 10%. Is that the same as 20% off?
remediationHint: Work the two steps out in ringgit on RM 100 and compare with a single 20% cut.

subject: mathematics
label: Converts between fractions, decimals and percentages by shifting the point at random
label_ms: Menukar pecahan, perpuluhan dan peratus dengan mengalih titik secara rawak
description: Writes 0.6 as 6% or 3/5 as 35%, applying a half-remembered shift without meaning.
correctReasoning: A percentage counts hundredths, so 0.6 is 60 hundredths, that is 60%.
diagnosticQuestion: Write 0.6 and 3/5 as percentages. Are they the same?
remediationHint: Use a 100-square grid and shade the amount before naming it.
